'''Paweł Kisielow''' (<small>Polish</small>: {{IPAc-pl|'|p|a|w|e|ł|-|k|i|'|ś|e|l|o|w}}; born 21 February 1945 in [[Gorlice]], Poland) is a Polish [[biologist]] who specializes in [[immunology]]. He is best known for his research on [[T cell]]s. He is a corresponding member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] and a member of the [[Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/scientist?id=66468&_k=kmjgw5 |language=pl |title=prof. dr hab. czł. koresp. PAN Paweł Kisielow |website=nauka-polska.pl |access-date=5 July 2024}}</ref>

==Career==
He graduated in [[biology]] from the [[Adam Mickiewicz University]] in [[Poznań]] and received a doctoral degree in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://teatrnn.pl/leksykon/artykuly/rodzina-kisielow/ |language=pl |title=Paweł Kisielow |website=teatrnn.pl |access-date=5 July 2024}}</ref> He became a professor in 1987. He works at the Hirszfeld Institute of Immunology and Experimental Therapy of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://pan.pl/czlonkowie/kisielow_pawel/ |language=pl |title=Paweł Kisielow |website=pan.pl |access-date=5 July 2024}}</ref>

In 1992, he received the [[Jurzykowski Prize]] conferred by the Alfred Jurzykowski Foundation in [[New York City|New York]].

In 1997, he was awarded the [[Körber European Science Prize]] jointly with [[Klaus Rajewsky]] and [[Harald von Boehmer]] for their work on mutant mouse models in clinical research. His scientific contributions have made significant progress towards better understanding the defense system leading to the development of treatments to support a weakened [[immune system]], to combat 
[[cancer]] and to deal with [[autoimmune disease]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://koerber-stiftung.de/site/assets/files/18911/koerber_prize_1997_mutant_mouse_models_in_clinical_research.pdf |title=Körber European Science Prize 1997 |website=koerber-stiftung.de |access-date=5 July 2024}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.koerber-stiftung.de/wissenschaft/koerber-preis-fuer-die-europaeische-wissenschaft/bisherige-preistraeger/bis-2004/1997.html |language=de |title=Körber-Preis für die Europäische Wissenschaft 1997 |website=koerber-stiftung.de |access-date=5 July 2024 |archive-date=6 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306190457/http://www.koerber-stiftung.de/wissenschaft/koerber-preis-fuer-die-europaeische-wissenschaft/bisherige-preistraeger/bis-2004/1997.html |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

In 2003, he became the recipient of the [[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] Award for his outstanding scientific output.

==Selected publications==
*''How does the immune system learn to distinguish between good and evil? The first definitive studies of T cell central tolerance and positive selection'' (2019)<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Pawel-Kisielow-38253173 |title=Pawel Kisielow's research while affiliated with Polish Academy of Sciences and other places |website=researchgate.net |access-date=5 July 2024}}</ref>
*''The evolutionary conservation of the bidirectional activity of the NWC gene promoter in jawed vertebrates and the domestication of the RAG transposon'' (with Lukasz Sniezewski, Sylwia Janik, Agnieszka Łaszkiewicz, Malgorzata Cebrat, 2017)<ref name="auto1" />
*''Anti-GITR Antibody Treatment Increases TCR Repertoire Diversity of Regulatory but not Effector T Cells Engaged in the Immune Response Against B16 Melanoma'' (with Bozena Scirka, Edyta Anna Szurek, Maciej Pietrzak, Arkadiusz Miazek, 2017)<ref name="auto1" />
*''Search for the Function of NWC, Third Gene Within RAG Locus: Generation and Characterization of NWC-Deficient Mice'' (with Monika Kasztura, Lukasz Sniezewski, Agnieszka Łaszkiewicz, 2015)<ref name="auto1" />
